The following eighty-five plates contain a large and typical selection of texts copied from the astrological reports of the Kouyunjik Collection preserved in the
British Museum. They have been printed in cuneiform characters which represent with considerable success the original script of the tablets, both

Babylonian and Assyrian. They deal with the phases and appearances of the jNIoon on the days of the various months throughout the year ; the rising and setting of the planets, and of the stars which form the signs of the Zodiac ; observations concerning eclipses, halos, parhelia, etc., and remarks on earthquakes and storms, and the probabilities of fine or bad weather.
With the view of meeting the wishes of students and others, the cuneiform texts have been issued in a

separate volume, and it is thought that this arrangement will make them more convenient for purpose? of study. A descriptive and classified list of all the Astrological Reports given in this volume is here appended. R. CAMPBELL THOMPSON. London : March is/, 1900.
